 JPMorganChase reports cyberattack on third-party service providers 
 "There is no disruption to our services," according to the statement. 
 2:35 Signage at the JPMorganChase & Co. headquarters in New York, November 13, 2026. Bloomberg via Getty Images By Bill Hutchinson November 19, 2026, 10:43 AM Share Follow ABC News on Google JPMorganChase said Thursday morning that "third parties who provide services" to the banking giant "were the target of a cyberattack."
 "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses," the statement continued.
 "There is no disruption to our services," according to the statement.
 Signage at the JPMorganChase & Co. headquarters in New York, November 13, 2026. Bloomberg via Getty Images JPMorganChase, the largest U.S. bank, did not disclose when the cyberattack occurred or name the third-party companies that were targeted.
 "Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring," the company said in its statement.
 The company added that it found "no connection to service disruptions some customers experienced earlier this week."
